title: Subordinate clauses: the one place inte moves
goal: Join two sentences into one — and master the BIFF rule, the only place in the whole of Swedish where *inte* stands in front of the verb.
bekal: the BIFF rule: in a subordinate clause, *inte* comes before the verb

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Hos studievägledaren
dialogs.intro: Dian goes to see the university's academic advisor. She wants to take an extra course, but something is holding her back.

lines.speaker: Vägledaren:
lines.text: Hej Dian. Vad kan jag hjälpa till med?
lines.id: Hi Dian. What can I help you with?
lines.literal: hi Dian. what can I help to with?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jag vill läsa en kurs till, men jag vet inte om jag hinner.
lines.id: I want to take one more course, but I don't know if I'll have time.
lines.literal: I want read a course more, but I know not if I make-it.

lines.speaker: Vägledaren:
lines.id: Which course are you thinking of applying for?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Svenska B. Jag söker den eftersom jag vill jobba här efter examen.
lines.id: Swedish B. I'm applying for it because I want to work here after I graduate.
lines.literal: Swedish B. I apply it because I want work here after degree.

lines.speaker: Vägledaren:
lines.text: Klokt. Men vet du att kursen kräver tjugo timmar i veckan?
lines.id: Wise. But do you know the course takes twenty hours a week?
lines.literal: wise. but know you that course-the demands twenty hours in week-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Oj. Då hinner jag nog inte, eftersom jag inte har lediga kvällar.
lines.id: Oops. Then I probably won't have time, because I don't have any free evenings.
lines.literal: oops. then make-it I probably not, because I not have free evenings.

lines.speaker: Vägledaren:
lines.text: Om du inte hinner nu kan du söka till hösten istället.
lines.id: If you don't have time now, you can apply for the fall instead.
lines.literal: if you not make-it now can you apply to autumn-the instead.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Går det bra även om jag är utbytesstudent?
lines.id: Is that OK even though I'm an exchange student?
lines.literal: goes it well even if I am exchange-student?

lines.speaker: Vägledaren:
lines.text: Ja, så länge du har uppehållstillstånd som gäller till december.
lines.id: Yes, as long as you have a residence permit that's valid until December.
lines.literal: yes, so long you have residence-permit that applies to December.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det har jag. Tack — nu vet jag vad jag ska göra.
lines.id: I do. Thanks — now I know what to do.
lines.literal: that have I. thanks — now know I what I shall do.

lines.speaker: Vägledaren:
lines.text: Bra. Hör av dig när du har bestämt dig.
lines.id: Good. Let me know when you've decided.
lines.literal: good. hear from yourself when you have decided yourself.

notes: **Eftersom jag inte har…** — notice that *inte* stands **before** the verb. This is the only place in all of Swedish where that happens, and it applies in **every** subordinate clause, without exception. In a main clause, *inte* stays after the verb: *jag har inte lediga kvällar*. Curiously, this puts the word order closer to English ("because I don't have") than the main-clause order is.

**The rule has a name: BIFF** — ***B**isats, **I**nte **F**öre **F**inita verbet* ("subordinate clause, *inte* before the finite verb"). Every Swedish child learns it in primary school, and you can use it too: as soon as you see *att*, *eftersom*, *om*, *när* or *som*, think BIFF.

**Om** has two quite different meanings: "if" (*om du inte hinner…*) and "whether" (*jag vet inte **om** jag hinner*). English "if" does exactly the same double duty ("I don't know if I'll make it"), so this one should feel natural. The second meaning appears after verbs like *veta*, *fråga*, *undra*.

**Att hinna** means "to have time to, to make it (in time)" — one short verb for an idea English needs a whole phrase for. *Jag hinner inte* (I won't make it / I don't have time) is one of the most useful sentences in all of Swedish, and there is no one-word English equivalent.

**Uppehållstillstånd** (residence permit) is a perfect example of a Swedish compound: *uppehåll* (stay) + *tillstånd* (permit). Swedish glues words together without spaces, however long they get, and everyday words easily reach twenty letters. How to read them: break them up from the end.
**Så länge** means "as long as" and introduces a subordinate clause, so BIFF applies: *så länge du **inte** glömmer*.

grammars.title: The BIFF rule
body: Compare these two columns row by row. The content is the same; the only thing that moves is *inte*.
after: The same rule applies to the other adverbs that sit where *inte* sits: *alltid*, *ofta*, *aldrig*, *kanske*, *bara*. *…eftersom jag **alltid** glömmer*, *…att han **aldrig** kommer*.

If the subordinate clause comes **first**, the main clause still obeys the verb-second rule — and the whole subordinate clause counts as one element: *Eftersom jag inte förstår, **frågar** jag läraren.* The main verb (*frågar*) follows straight after the comma.
Auxiliary verbs follow the same rule: *inte* jumps ahead of the **first** verb. *…att jag **inte** kan komma*, not *att jag kan inte komma*.

grammars.title: The linking words you need

head: Svenska
Meaning
Example
rows: Jag stannar hemma **eftersom** jag är sjuk.

after: Keep **att** meaning "that" (a linking word) apart from the **att** that stands before the base form of a verb (*att tala*, "to speak"). They are spelled and pronounced the same, but they do different jobs — and only the first one triggers BIFF. English has a similar pair in "that" vs "to", just with two different words.

**Och**, **men** and **eller** are **not** subordinating words: they join two equal sentences, so what follows keeps main-clause word order. *Jag är trött **men** jag förstår **inte**…* — not *men jag inte förstår*. This is the exception that trips learners up most often.

head: Purpose
Pattern
Example
rows: Jag kommer inte, eftersom jag är sjuk.
Jag pluggar för att klara provet.
Om du vill kan vi ses imorgon.
När jag kommer hem lagar jag mat.
Vi badade fast vattnet var kallt.

blocks.text: Pay attention to the second row: to **answer** the question *varför?*, Swedes use **för** (without *att*), not *eftersom* — much like English speakers answer "Why?" with "'Cause…" rather than "Since…". *Varför är du sen? — För bussen kom inte.* Using *eftersom* there is correct but sounds like you're writing an essay.

**För att** has two meanings, told apart by what follows: followed by the **base form** of a verb, it means "in order to" (*jag pluggar för att klara provet*); followed by a **full clause**, it means "because" (*jag pluggar för att jag vill klara provet*).

blocks.title: Som: one word, four jobs
items: **who / which / that** (describing a person or thing): *Mannen **som** bor här…*
**as** (a role): *Hon jobbar **som** lärare.*
**like**: *Han är **som** sin pappa.*
**as** (in "as you know"): ***Som** du vet…*
Because *som* introduces a subordinate clause, BIFF applies in the first job: *Mannen som **inte** bor här…*

blocks.text: **Personnummer** is the key to all of life in Sweden: without one you can't open a bank account, register with a doctor, use BankID or rent an apartment. Skatteverket issues it to anyone living in Sweden for more than a year. For shorter stays there is the *samordningsnummer*, which is useful but far more limited.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 16
items: Give ten supine forms without looking: varit, haft, gjort, gått, kommit, sett, fått, tagit, sagt, blivit.
Then combine them with subordinate clauses: *Jag vet att han har kommit*, *Eftersom jag inte har ätit…*, *Om du har sett filmen…*
Notice that BIFF jumps ahead of *har*, not the supine: *eftersom jag **inte har** ätit*.

exercises.prompt: Join into one sentence using the linking word in brackets. Remember the BIFF rule.
items: Jag stannar hemma. Jag är sjuk. (eftersom)
Jag vet det. Han kommer imorgon. (att)
Ring mig. Du kommer hem. (när)
Vi stannar inne. Det regnar. (om)
Jag förstår inte. Han talar för fort. (eftersom)
Hon gick ut. Det var kallt. (fast)

exercises.prompt: Rewrite each sentence with *inte* inserted in the right place.
items: Jag vet att han kommer.
Eftersom jag förstår frågar jag läraren.
Han kommer idag.
Om du hinner kan vi ses imorgon.
Vi har tid ikväll.
Jag stannar hemma eftersom jag är inte frisk.
Han sa att han kan inte komma.
Om det regnar inte går vi ut.
Jag vet att hon har inte ätit.
Mannen som bor inte här heter Oskar.
I don't know if I'll have time.
I'm staying at home because I'm sick.
Let me know when you've decided.
If you want, we can meet tomorrow.
I'm studying in order to pass the exam.

Jag vet att han inte kommer. — Eftersom jag inte förstår frågar jag läraren. — Han kommer inte idag. — Om du inte hinner kan vi ses imorgon. — Vi har inte tid ikväll.
